newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ICC Bank yr pretax profit 9.08 mln.
newsitem.headline: ICC Bank yr pretax profit 9.08 mln.

text.p: Ireland's ICC Bank said on Monday that it made pre-tax profits of 9.08 million punts in the year ended October 31, 1996 against 12.01 the previous year.
The state-owned bank said operating profits were up 8.4 percent to 13.03 million pounds against 12.02 million in 1995.
Underlying profits were up 15.4 percent when account was taken of non-recurring items, the bank said.
The accounts included a one-off exceptional charge of 3.95 million pounds in respect of reorganisation costs.
Earnings per share were 58.9 pence and a final dividend of 15.0 pence per share was proposed, the bank said in a statement, representing an unchanged distribution for the year of 2.52 million pounds.

"We recorded growth in all areas of business last year, achieving the broad objectives we set for the Bank. These were increasing profitability, achieving quality growth and building a platform for the long term development of the Bank," Chairman Phil Flynn said in a statement.

"The economic outlook for the current year continues to be positive and ICC bank intends to maximise the opportunities this presents bothfor itself and for our customers," Managing Director Micahel Quinn said.
Competititon is intense, putting continuing pressure on margins, but we will operate on a targeted niche basis to maximise the value we offer," he added.
Flynn said the management team planned to grow the bank significantly over the next four years and would examine strategic approaches to expand and develop the business base.
